image_description: Two adult male mallard ducks (drakes) standing in shallow water. The duck on the left displays the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, and grey body. The duck on the right appears to be in eclipse plumage or a different lighting angle, showing a brownish head but retaining the yellow bill and orange legs. Both are partially submerged with visible webbed feet.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects clearly exhibit the broad, flat, yellow-green bills characteristic of mallard drakes.
Dark eyes are visible on both subjects, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bodies appear robust and streamlined. The plumage texture looks dense and water-resistant, sitting correctly on the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left subject perfectly matches the 'iridescent green head with white neck ring' description. The right subject shows variation but remains consistent with male mallard morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Orange legs and webbed feet are clearly visible beneath the water surface. The anatomy (webbing between toes) is structurally correct and distinct.
Folded wings are visible along the sides of the bodies, appearing broad and properly integrated into the shoulder structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers is visible on the rear of both ducks.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the webbed feet. AI often struggles with the specific geometry of webbing between toes. Verify if the feet look like solid orange blobs or distinct toes with connecting skin. Also, check the reflection of the green head on the water; it should be distorted by ripples, not a perfect mirror image.
